gap: No result ChatGPT got turns the makers' sunlight claims into one comparable figure. eufy's '2 hours of sun' for the SoloCam S340 rests on a harvest of 800–1,200 mAh a day against 100–200 mAh of use, so it carries a 4–12× margin. Reolink's '20 minutes with the 3 W panel' (Argus PT Ultra) works out to only about 1 Wh at the panel's rated output, and Tapo's '50 minutes' (C465) is measured at lab standard sun of 1,000 W/m² with up to 100 events a day. The gap between 2 hours and 20 minutes comes from how each maker builds its claim, not from a 6× difference in panels. Also, every maker's charging floor is 32°F, even where the camera is rated to run at -4°F.
standout_why: I read homegearlab, VisionBay, SafeWise, Bob Vila, thebrickfantastic and rottenwifi. VisionBay and thebrickfantastic copy the raw sun-minute claims (Reolink 20 min, Tapo 45 min, eufy 2–3 h) with no common baseline, and VisionBay says it sets none. Homegearlab quotes eufy's 450–900 mAh/day harvest for the S3 Pro only, never for the S340 or against another brand, and lists the S340's -4°F to 122°F range without saying whether it covers charging. SafeWise (cited) says solar cameras 'probably won't charge below 32º F' as a general hedge. No page gives each maker's own 32°F charging floor next to its -4°F operating rating. No rival puts Reolink's mixed battery units (mAh on the Argus 4 Pro, Wh on the Eco Ultra and PT Ultra) on one basis, and none points out that eufy and Reolink both quote battery life at 300 s of recording a day.
decides: This backs the S340 and Argus 4 Pro picks. It removes a false tie-breaker: a shopper shouldn't choose the Argus PT Ultra over the S340 because '20 minutes' sounds better than '2 hours'. The claims are built on different margins and conditions. On the same 300 s/day basis that both makers use, the S340 (10,000 mAh, 3 months) lasts longer on battery alone than the Argus 4 Pro (5,000 mAh, about 2 months), and that reserve is what matters when the panel can't charge. For buyers where winters freeze, the 32°F floor from eufy, Reolink and TP-Link means no panel size will charge a frozen camera. Battery reserve and a sunny, south-facing mount matter more than panel watts.
candidates: Reolink Argus 4 Pro + Solar Panel 2 (6 W)

findings.label: Maker sunlight claim
findings.value: 2 hours of direct sun a day for continuous power, with a 2.2 W removable panel
findings.source_title: eufy SoloCam S340 Outdoor Security Camera - eufy US
findings.note: Quoted: 'Adjustable and Removable 2.2W Solar Panel' and '2 hours of direct sunlight daily is enough to stay continuously powered.' At rated output, 2.2 W × 2 h = 4.4 Wh.

findings.label: Maker harvest vs consumption per day
findings.value: 800–1,200 mAh collected a day in optimal sun vs 100–200 mAh used in a day and night of average use
findings.source_title: eufy SoloCam S340 - 3K FHD Dual Solar Powered Security Camera - eufy US
findings.note: Both figures are in mAh, so the ratio needs no voltage assumption. Harvest ÷ use = 800/200 = 4× at worst and 1,200/100 = 12× at best. The 2-hour claim therefore carries a large built-in margin. In the same terms, the camera's daily use would need roughly 10–20 min of optimal sun.
